name: Puerto Princesa International Airport / PAF Antonio Bautista Air Base
before:
The airport for Puerto Princesa in Palawan, and the main gateway to the Puerto Princesa Underground River, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the New 7 Wonders of Nature.

The terminal is newer and larger than the destination's reputation suggests. A 13,000 square metre two-level building rated for two million passengers a year replaced an old 3,000 square metre terminal that could handle only 350,000. Six aircraft bays take aircraft as large as an A330, A350 or 787, there are two lounges, parking for 200 cars and free wifi since 2019.

The single 2,601 metre runway is shared with Antonio Bautista Air Base and is equipped with an instrument landing system and approach lighting.
after:
The airport for Puerto Princesa in Palawan, and the one to fly into for the Puerto Princesa Underground River, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the New 7 Wonders of Nature.

Its apron takes aircraft as large as an Airbus A330.

The single runway, about 2,600 metres long, is shared with Antonio Bautista Air Base.
